#WebCodecs

WebCodecs in Wren is native: the pixel model, the sample layouts, the format conversions and the memory accounting live in the host (Odin), and the decoders wire to the existing media pipeline (src/media) and image decoders (src/images). The JavaScript surface is thin glue in native/js/runtime/web_webcodecs*.c; no part of the API runs in interpreted JavaScript.

#What is implemented

InterfaceWhereNotes
VideoFramesrc/page/webcodecs_frame.odin, bindings_webcodecs.odinfrom a canvas / image / video / ImageBitmap / OffscreenCanvas / VideoFrame / BufferSource; copyTo, allocationSize, visibleRect, colorSpace, clone, close; drawable and transferable
VideoColorSpaceweb_webcodecs.cthe four nullable members, toJSON
ImageDecoder, ImageTrackList, ImageTrackbindings_image_decoder.odindecodes with src/images; decode({frameIndex}), tracks, honest isTypeSupported
EncodedVideoChunk, EncodedAudioChunkwebcodecs_chunks.odinimmutable coded samples; copyTo, byteLength
AudioDatawebcodecs_chunks.odinPCM in any AudioSampleFormat; planar / interleaved copyTo, allocationSize, clone, close
VideoDecoderbindings_video_decoder.odinwires to src/media (H.264, VP9, AV1); honest isConfigSupported
AudioDecoderbindings_audio_decoder.odinwires to src/media (AAC, MP3, Opus, FLAC)
VideoEncoder, AudioEncoderbindings_encoders.odinhonest: no encoder is linked, so isConfigSupported is false and configure raises NotSupportedError

#Memory and preferences

Every frame, chunk and AudioData is charged against page.max_fetch_bytes, like any other buffer, and freed with the object or the page. about:config:

  • webcodecs.enabled — the whole API (off hides the interfaces).
  • webcodecs.max_frame_bytes — the pixels (or samples) of one VideoFrame / AudioData.
  • webcodecs.max_dimension — the largest side of a VideoFrame.
  • webcodecs.max_decode_queue — the most encoded chunks a decoder may have queued (decodeQueueSize).
  • webcodecs.allow_encoders — the encoders (always honest-unsupported today).

#Notes and limits

  • VideoDecoder output needs CPU planes. The software decoders (VP9, AV1) produce CPU planes that are wrapped directly as I420 / NV12 VideoFrames. A GPU-only picture (DXVA H.264 into a Direct3D texture) cannot be read back from the page layer; configure asks the backend for a software decoder, and a decoded picture that still has no CPU planes is reported through the error callback. A software H.264 path (or a GPU read-back) would lift this.
  • The decode is synchronous on the page thread (the inputs are bounded and the built-in decoders are memory-safe); the decode/flush promises and the output callbacks still run as their own event-loop turns.
  • VideoFrame transfer across realms (postMessage to a worker) moves the pixels through a process-wide host token (VideoFrame_takeForTransfer / adoptTransfer), wired into structured clone (native/js/runtime/clone.c, tag T_VIDEO_FRAME): the pixels never cross a heap boundary as a JS value.
  • ImageDecoder data accepts a BufferSource or a Blob; a ReadableStream source is not read here (read it to bytes first).
  • Encoders are intentionally unsupported until a pure-Rust encoder (rav1e, a VP8/VP9 encoder, or an Opus encoder) is added to native/Cargo.toml; bindings_encoders.odin is the single place to wire it.
